name: Memory Safety & Exploitation
description: Memory-corruption bugs, exploitation techniques, and mitigations (ASLR, CFI, sanitizers).
narrative:
The earliest papers in this slice show memory-safety research branching out from the classic "corrupt memory in a desktop C/C++ program" model into new attack surfaces. A cluster of 2018 work pushed fuzzing into hard-to-reach targets, with "IoTFuzzer: Discovering Memory Corruptions in IoT Through App-based Fuzzing" (NDSS 2018) and "What You Corrupt Is Not What You Crash" (NDSS 2018) wrestling with embedded devices where crashes are silent and feedback is scarce. At the same time, the defensive community kept refining control-flow integrity and code reuse defenses — "Enforcing Unique Code Target Property for Control-Flow Integrity" (CCS 2018) and "Compiler-Assisted Code Randomization" (S&P 2018) tightened CFI and diversification — while attackers showed those defenses were not enough, with "Block Oriented Programming: Automating Data-Only Attacks" (CCS 2018) demonstrating that data-only attacks sidestep CFI entirely. A parallel "exploitability" thread emerged, where the question shifted from "is there a bug?" to "can it be weaponized?", driven by "FUZE" (USENIX 2018) for kernel use-after-free and "Revery: From Proof-of-Concept to Exploitable" (CCS 2018).

The pivotal shift came in 2019 when hardware-level flaws moved to center stage. "Spectre Attacks: Exploiting Speculative Execution" (S&P 2019) — by far the most-cited paper here — showed the CPU's own microarchitecture could leak memory across security boundaries, reframing memory safety as a hardware as well as a software problem. Rowhammer matured along the same lines: after "Another Flip in the Wall of Rowhammer Defenses" (S&P 2018), researchers broke supposedly safe configurations with "Exploiting Correcting Codes: ECC Memory Against Rowhammer" (S&P 2019) and "SPOILER" (USENIX 2019). 2019 was also a strong year for taking stock and for isolation: the SoK papers "SoK: Sanitizing for Security" (S&P 2019) and "SoK: Shining Light on Shadow Stacks" (S&P 2019) systematized the defensive toolbox, while "ERIM: Secure, Efficient In-process Isolation with Protection Keys (MPK)" (USENIX 2019) popularized cheap intra-process isolation via Intel MPK.

From 2020 onward the field consolidated around three durable themes. First, intra-process isolation became a research industry of its own — "Donky" (USENIX 2020) and "xMP" (S&P 2020) extended the MPK idea, even as "PKU Pitfalls" (USENIX 2020) showed these schemes can be attacked, mirroring the earlier attack-defense arms race in CFI. Second, trusted execution environments inherited classic memory bugs, with "A Tale of Two Worlds" (CCS 2019) and "TeeRex" (USENIX 2020) finding memory corruption inside SGX enclaves, and "Towards Memory Safe Enclave Programming with Rust-SGX" (CCS 2019) pointing to safe languages as the fix. Third, automated kernel exploitation kept advancing through "SLAKE" (CCS 2019), "KEPLER" (USENIX 2019), and "KOOBE" (USENIX 2020).

Where things stand now reflects two converging answers. On the software side, the agenda has clearly turned toward fundamentally safe foundations — hardware-enforced capabilities in "Cornucopia: Temporal Safety for CHERI Heaps" (S&P 2020) and safe-language tooling in "MirChecker: Detecting Bugs in Rust Programs via Static Analysis" (CCS 2021) — rather than only patching unsafe C. On the hardware side, the threats keep evolving faster than mitigations: Rowhammer defenses keep falling to "SMASH" (USENIX 2021), "BLACKSMITH" (S&P 2022), and "Half-Double" (USENIX 2022), and speculative execution attacks persist with "RETBLEED" (USENIX 2022). The arc of this list runs from classic software memory corruption toward an arms race that now spans the silicon itself, with safe languages and hardware capabilities as the most promising long-term escapes.

milestones.title: IoTFuzzer: Discovering Memory Corruptions in IoT Through App-based Fuzzing
milestones.note: pushed memory-corruption discovery onto IoT firmware via app-driven fuzzing, opening the embedded attack surface

milestones.title: Block Oriented Programming: Automating Data-Only Attacks
milestones.note: showed automated data-only attacks bypass deployed control-flow integrity, undercutting the dominant defense

milestones.title: Spectre Attacks: Exploiting Speculative Execution
milestones.note: by far the most-cited work here, it reframed memory safety as a microarchitectural problem

milestones.title: SoK: Sanitizing for Security
milestones.note: systematized the sanitizer/defense landscape, giving the field a shared map of mitigations and gaps

milestones.title: ERIM: Secure, Efficient In-process Isolation with Protection Keys (MPK)
milestones.note: popularized cheap MPK-based intra-process isolation that seeded a whole line of follow-on work

milestones.title: Cornucopia: Temporal Safety for CHERI Heaps
milestones.note: advanced hardware-capability (CHERI) enforcement of temporal memory safety as a fundamental fix

milestones.title: MirChecker: Detecting Bugs in Rust Programs via Static Analysis
milestones.note: marked the shift toward safe-language tooling, hunting residual bugs even in Rust

milestones.title: BLACKSMITH: Scalable Rowhammering in the Frequency Domain
milestones.note: broke modern in-DRAM TRR defenses, showing the Rowhammer arms race still favors attackers
